sections.h2: How does selling a house in Midland, MI work?
sections.html:
Midland sellers choose between a listing, a sale on their own, and a cash purchase, then close through a title company and record the deed with Midland County. Because the city runs its own rental certification and tax calendar, a few local steps sit on top of the state ones.

The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate for Midland is 42,806 people, up 0.3% from the 2020 base. The city covers 34.37 square miles of land, which is why density is only about 1,238 people per square mile. For 2020 to 2024 the Census counted 18,535 households, 67.1% of them owner-occupied, a median owner-occupied value of $203,900 and a median gross rent of $1,048.

Median household income is $73,325 and 44.6% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or more. The poverty rate is 10.3%, and the mean commute is 20 minutes.

sections.h2: What is Midland like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Midland is the Midland County seat, built where the Chippewa River meets the Tittabawassee, about 24 miles northwest of Saginaw and 19 miles west of Bay City. Dow Chemical was founded here in 1897 and still has its world headquarters in the city.

That employer shapes the housing demand. Dow's Michigan Operations Industrial Park covers 2,600 acres along the Bay City Road corridor and supports roughly 6,000 employees and contractors across tenants such as Corteva Agriscience, Hemlock Semiconductor and DuPont. Health care is the third large sector, led by a 324-bed MyMichigan hospital, and Northwood University anchors higher education. Midland Public Schools and Bullock Creek Public Schools are the public districts named for the area.

The city lists more than 35 neighborhoods grouped into eight general areas:

  • Downtown and the historic Circle, dating from 1938
  • North Side and Midland West, with parks, mature trees and river access
  • Country Club, known for large wooded lots
  • East End, where a Midtown revitalization began in 2018
  • Industrial Park and the small South area near the old Mapleton depot
  • West Main Street Historic District, set up in 1979

Houses inside that historic district fall under a commission that must approve construction, additions, alterations, repairs and moves, so ask before you plan work for a sale. US-10 runs along the northern edge, M-20 heads west toward Mount Pleasant, and M-47 links to Saginaw and MBS International Airport. Midland has no regular scheduled bus, only Dial-A-Ride inside the city.

sections.h2: How does Midland's 2020 flood affect a sale?
sections.html:
It affects it as a question buyers ask. On May 19, 2020, the Edenville and Sanford dams failed and about 10,000 Midland residents were told to evacuate, in what was called a 500-year flood.

If your house took water or sits near the rivers, pull together the repair invoices, permits, insurance claims and any remediation records before you list or ask for an offer. Documented repairs are easier to price than a basement that nobody can explain.

Midland averages 33.41 inches of precipitation and 31.4 inches of snow a year, with January highs near 29 degrees, so roofs, gutters and furnaces get a real test every winter.

sections.h2: Does Midland inspect rental houses before they are sold or leased?
sections.html:
Midland inspects and certifies every home, duplex, rooming house, short-term rental and apartment that the owner does not occupy, and a unit cannot be rented out until it is certified. The rule covers houses where no rent is collected and where the tenant is a relative.

An owner living in a single-family home may take up to two boarders without an inspection. More than two renters triggers one, and no more than four unrelated tenants may share a rental unit. The fee schedule that took effect July 1, 2025 is:

  • Rooming house: $105
  • Other rental units: $79 for the first unit and $36 for each additional unit
  • First reinspection per unit: no charge, and each additional one costs the same as the certification fee
  • Late certification: $36 per unit, plus the full certification fee again after 30 and 60 days

The Rental Program answers questions at (989) 837-3383, option 1, or rentalprogram@midland-mi.org. A house you rent for a few months before selling will need its certificate first.

sections.h2: What are the Midland property tax dates a seller should know?
sections.html:
Midland bills twice a year, with summer bills mailed July 1 and winter bills mailed December 1, and the city lists the full calendar on its own page. Tax Day is December 31, so the condition and ownership of the property on that date set the next year's value.

Midland tax calendar
DateWhat happens
February 14Prior year's winter taxes due without penalty
March 1Delinquent real property taxes go to the Midland County Treasurer
2nd Monday in MarchBoard of Review hears value and classification appeals
June 1Principal residence exemption affidavit deadline for the summer bill
September 15Summer taxes due; deferment filing deadline
November 1Principal residence exemption affidavit deadline for the winter bill

Source: City of Midland, Important Tax Related Dates. A buyer who owns and occupies the house by June 1 can qualify for the exemption on the summer bill, and one who does so by November 1 qualifies for the winter bill. Under MCL 211.27a the taxable value resets the year after a sale, so the new owner's bill is usually higher than yours.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed in Midland County cost?
sections.html:
The standard recording fee in Midland County is $30 per document, no matter how many pages. The Register of Deeds is at 220 W Ellsworth Street and open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

  • A warranty deed or land contract needs a $5 tax certificate showing taxes are current.
  • State and county transfer tax is charged on the sale amount, at $3.75 plus 55 cents per $500 of value.
  • Copies cost $1 per page, and certifying a copy is $5 plus $1 per page.
  • The office accepts e-recording for most documents, but court orders and death certificates need a raised seal and cannot be filed electronically.
  • The office does not prepare deeds or give legal advice, so use a title company or attorney.

Deeds that pass between a parent and child or grandparent and grandchild are exempt from the state transfer tax under MCL 207.526.

sections.h2: How can I sell a Midland house fast?
sections.html:
Choose by timeline and condition. A listing suits a house in good shape with time to spare, a sale by owner suits someone willing to do the work, and a cash purchase suits a house with a tenant, damage from the 2020 flood or an unfinished rental certification.

Send us the Midland address and we will make an offer based on how the house looks today. Compare it with what a listing would net after repairs and fees.

faqs.q: Can I rent out my Midland house while I try to sell it?
faqs.a: Yes, but only after the city has inspected and certified it. The certification fee is $79 for the first unit, and late certification adds $36 per unit.

faqs.q: When must a Midland buyer file for the principal residence exemption?
faqs.a: By June 1 for the summer bill and November 1 for the winter bill, provided the buyer owns and occupies the house by that date. The affidavit is filed with the city.

faqs.q: Where do delinquent Midland property taxes go?
faqs.a: To the Midland County Treasurer. Real property taxes still unpaid on March 1 are turned over to the county for collection.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Midland County?
faqs.a: The recording fee is $30 per document, plus $5 for a tax certificate on a warranty deed. Transfer tax is charged separately on the sale price.

faqs.q: Does the 2020 flood still matter when selling a house in Midland?
faqs.a: It can, if your house took water or sits near the Chippewa or Tittabawassee. Collect repair and insurance records, because buyers and lenders ask about that event.
